memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then food was set before him, but he said, 'I will not eat until I have told you what I have to say.' 'Then tell us,' Laban said. So he said, 'I am Abraham's servant. The LORD has blessed my master abundantly, and he has become wealthy. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys. My master's wife Sarah has borne him a son in her old age, and he has given him everything he owns. And my master made me swear an oath, and said, "You must not get a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live, but go to my father's family and to my own clan, and get a wife for my son." Then I asked my master, "What if the woman will not come back with me?" He replied, "The LORD, before whom I have walked faithfully, will send his angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you can get a wife for my son from my own clan and from my father's family. You will be released from my oath if, when you go to my clan, they refuse to give her to you—then you will be released from my oath."'" - Gen 24:33-41 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The food is ready and the servant is surely tired and hungry after a long journey — yet he refuses to eat until he has completed his mission. "I will not eat until I have told you what I have to say." His master's business comes before his own comfort.

What a picture of faithfulness. This servant is not even named in the chapter, yet he serves with a whole heart, treating his master's concerns as his own. He could have relaxed, enjoyed the meal, and raised the matter later. Instead, duty comes first.

There is something Christlike here. Jesus once told His disciples, "My food is to do the will of him who sent me" (John 4:34). The servant's single-mindedness reminds us that doing the Father's will can be more satisfying than bread itself.

Notice too how the servant retells the story — he begins with what God has done for Abraham. His testimony centres on God's faithfulness, not his own effort.

Where has comfort quietly taken priority over the work God has given you? Sometimes love means finishing the task before we sit down to rest. Ask God for a faithful, wholehearted spirit like this servant's — one that puts first things first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has my comfort taken priority over the task God has given me?
2. Am I as faithful in unseen service as this unnamed servant?
3. Does doing God's will satisfy me more than my own ease?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a faithful, wholehearted spirit that puts Your work before my own comfort. Let doing Your will be my deepest satisfaction. Amen.
